verdict_on_present:
What it gets right. (1) The grain and the names: a person recognises "holds itself in place" with one everyday example, and Ren did. (2) Every mark is traced to a Lean statement and was put to a second reader; line style carries how far seen; the unresolved are kept. (3) "stays", "inside" and "leads-out" are already the beginning of typed changes. Keep all of it.

What it is. A picture of STATES (boxes and moves between them) with no picture of the STRUCTURE that generates them. And the 15 are not states of one thing. They answer five different questions about one small structure: where the rule comes from (fixed-rule, holds-itself, judged-inside, checkers-inside); whether bending it is picked (shaping-costs, shaping-pays); how many ways are in use (several-ways, all-on-one); what is used up (uncounted, ended); who has a say and when (felt, noticers-gone, cost-counts, past-turning-back). A flat list puts five axes in one plane. The prototype's own numbers show the cost: of 88 items only 38 (43%) become marks between places; 31 (16 inside, 15 stays) are true and have nowhere to be drawn, 12 of the 16 inside one box (holds-itself); 19 have no home. The 38 arrows join only 16 ordered pairs of places. 12 of the 15 tests are worded about "the law", so they sort theorems; a person cannot apply them to a case. What makes the map faithful sits in about 27,700 words of notes on the 88 rows, which the picture cannot show.

Verdict. As a DATA STRUCTURE it is dominated: a structure exists from which this map can be regenerated (by forgetting two typed fields) and which also carries overlap, kinds of change, a case, and the holes. As a PICTURE at 15 places it is not dominated for recognition; at 35 to 40 it would be. It is not dominated on cost: it exists.
dominated_where: One arrow means four things, and a reader takes all four as 'this happens next'. (a) The run gets there by itself: a-code-formed-between-formations exit 1, several-ways to all-on-one (SharedCodes.agrees_every_start_iff). (b) A line between two sides, nothing shown crossing: the seven arrows between shaping-costs and shaping-pays (all exact iffs in cost against return), and unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure exits 1 and 6 (the adjudicator's note: 'a boundary for a fixed group, not a passage in time'). (c) The rule is changed from outside the run: closed-capture exit 1 (ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss; note: 'the theorem holds from any start ... not something the closed loop does by itself'). (d) Which of two times comes first: reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1. By the atlas's own fields (transition kind, exit drops) 8 of the 38 are lines, 4 are deadlines and 15 are exits that drop a premise.

One theorem, several arrows, and an origin that is not in the theorem. turned_by_loss is drawn from judged-inside (closed-capture exits 1 and 2) and again from holds-itself (a-counter-rule-read-from-its-own-share exit 2). Its statement holds from any start.

Overlap has no home. 'judged-inside is holds-itself with something not counted' exists only as two hand-set ties in layout.json. The condition 'held while an uncounted loss grows, the judging not drawn from the winners' (ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss; ChoiceCountCapture.counted_outlives_loss) 'fits none of the three tests cleanly'. PoolFromCourse.window_never_read is claimed by three tests. noticers-gone and all-on-one are 'one fact said two ways'.

Inner structure is invisible. Twelve thresholds and flips sit inside the one box holds-itself (a tipping count, its two sides, the pace of two rebuildings). shaping-pays and shaping-costs are each a side of that hold (DrawnShaping.critical_mass_iff), and the two-way arrow between them skips the two-sided hold that lies between.

A fork cannot be one item. reading-a-loss-in-time transition 1 has two equally exact heads (to felt, to past-turning-back); the second lives in a note. readers-drawn-from-the-selected transition 2 holds two iffs. The checker: 'one decision per item loses the second or hides it in a note'.

The layout carries a verdict the laws do not. It runs left to right from 'several ways' to 'the cost counts' (top right) and 'ended' (bottom). But loss-read-in-time-by-the-others exit 1 (ReadInTime.turned_iff) ends 'locked the other way': cost-counts is the same hold on its other side with the loss now registered. Drawn as two distant boxes they read as problem and remedy.

Use. The one real case (situations.json, a reward-model pipeline) is stored as a web: formations, couplings, readers, rule, time. The map is boxes with tests about laws. Nothing translates one into the other, so a case cannot be found on the map.

Scale. At 35 to 40 places and about 170 arrows a node-link picture stops being readable, and each new family reopens old tests: past-turning-back needs family A's point of no return; two family E cases sit on the costs/pays line; family F's alternation is the same lead-and-rule loop read late.
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Keep the places as names and stop treating them as the primitive. Underneath, hold the small structure that generates them: a handful of parts and the links between them. Say every place, every change and every case as answers to one short list of questions about those links ("Is the rule rebuilt from who is ahead?", "Does what is used up make a difference to anyone with a say?"). A PLACE is a named set of answers. A CHANGE is a law that turns one answer, marked by what turns it. A REAL CASE is the same questions answered for something actual. This is the theory's own grammar (formations, conditions, couplings; "a configuration is how it relates"), and situations.json already stores its case this way. Two pictures are drawn from it: the loop (what generates) and the key (where something can be and what can change). Ren's map is the second with its questions hidden, so it is kept and regenerated, not replaced.
schema:
Three primitives (part, question, law row); place and case are views.

parts[] (about 5 a region): things with a level or a membership.
- id, name {en, zh}.
- kind: amount | group | rule.

questions[] (about 9 a region): one question about a link between parts.
- id; ask {en, zh}: worded so a person can answer it of a case.
- about: [part, part], the link asked about.
- kind: wiring (the link is there or not) | measure (one quantity against another) | standing (where the run now is). Only standing changes by itself.
- sides: the named answers (two, sometimes three).
- premises: per side, ids in premises.json that state it (their holds_in / fails_in come along).
- line: the exact law where two sides meet at a proved threshold.
- same_as: a proved identity that puts another model's question on this one (the compose entries).
- late: the link is read after a delay (needed for family F).

places[]: a name for a set of answers.
- id, name, example (as now).
- where: {question: side}. This replaces the free-text test; the test is `where` read out.
- keeps: laws that say it stays (today's "stays" items). sets_in: laws that say how fast it is reached from any start.
- Containment and overlap between places are computed from `where`.

changes[]: one row per atlas item (the 88 unchanged) plus three fields.
- turns: the question whose answer changes; from, to (to may hold two sides: a fork).
- given: the answers the law needs; empty means from any start.
- by: itself (the run, in time) | chance | outside (a premise dropped: a link changed from outside the run) | none (a line: two sides compared, nothing shown crossing).
- law, strength, drops, source (dynamic, item): as now.

cases[]: something actual.
- names: its own nouns for the parts.
- answers: {question: side or "not known", with source}.
- Computed: the places it is in, the changes whose `given` it meets (what can happen next), the questions not answered (what is missing).
drawn_from_it:
1. THE LOOP (the five-minute picture; one per region, parts shared across regions). Parts as boxes, links as plain verbs. No plus and minus signs, no letters for loops. Line style is how far seen; a link that no law forms is dotted. Place names are written where they live: on a loop, on a link, at a cut link. Pressing a place lights the links that are on in it, so the 15 places are 15 lightings of one drawing and none stands above another. A real case is the same drawing with its own nouns. Each link shows which Lean models' laws take it, and a join between models is marked proved or a reading.

2. THE KEY (the hour picture; also the index of the articles and the questions to ask of a case). The questions in order, like a field guide's key: each fork a question, with its exact threshold where there is one; the leaves are the places. Changes are drawn by `by`: itself, an arrow; chance, a dotted arrow; outside, an arrow with a mark on the link that was changed; none, a shared border with no arrowhead. Positions come from the questions (column: which link; row: which side), not from a hand layout. With the forks hidden this is the map Ren said yes to.

Optional inset, only where a region has an exact line in two quantities: draw that line as a chart. For the hold: cost against the count of those ahead, DrawnShaping.critical_iff, three regimes (pays at every count; a tipping count with each side kept; costs at every count).
worked_sample:
PARTS (5). lead: who is ahead and by how much. rule: what the choosing goes by. say: those whose judgment enters the rule. store: something used up that others live on. dependants: those who live on it.

QUESTIONS (9), with ledger ids.
Q1 Is the rule rebuilt from who is ahead? [lead to rule; wiring] rulecapture-readsshare, taken by 5 of the region's dynamics.
Q2 Does the rebuilt rule favour whoever is ahead: at every lead / past a tipping count / the other side? [measure and standing] rulecapture-uniform; line DrawnShaping.critical_iff, ChoiceCountCapture.weighted_favours_iff.
Q3 Are those who judge the rule drawn from those ahead? [lead to say; wiring] closedcapture-drawn-pool.
Q4 Does going on use up something others live on? [to store] closedcapture-accrues, taken by 7.
Q5 Does what is used up make a difference to anyone with a say: never / not yet / yes? [store to say] closedcapture-unread, dropped by 5 exits; line Web.readOffCouplings_alike_iff. (Three sides is my reading of the items; v1's "uncounted" holds both never and not yet.)
Q6 Does it reach them before the point of no return? [measure, in time] line Web.readableInTime_iff (T < N); for the count of those ahead, ReadInTime.kept_early_iff and turned_iff.
Q7 Are those it would reach still among those asked? PoolFromCourse.window_never_read (K ≤ N).
Q8 Does bending the rule return to its doers at least what it costs? [measure] line RuleShaping.favours_iff (c ≤ s).
Q9 Does what is used up fall on those ahead themselves? [store to lead] PoolFromCourse borne_by_shapers_favours_iff.

PLACES as answers (9 of the 15).
- A rule set from outside = {Q1 no}. keeps: Law.perturbation_reabsorbed (target-capture, which has no item in v1).
- Holds itself in place = {Q1 yes, Q2 favours}. keeps: RuleCapture.locked_stays. sets_in: uniform_locks. Inner line: Q2's tipping count, where 12 of v1's "inside" items live.
- Drawing on what is not counted = {Q4 yes, Q5 never or not yet}. keeps: standingCount_unselected (readings-revised-spread-and-locked exit 3).
- Judged only from inside = Holds itself + {Q3 yes, Q4 yes, Q5 never}. Containment is computed. Marked: no single law carries all four answers (the closed-capture checker's remark).
- Felt by someone with a say = {Q4 yes, Q5 yes, Q6 before}.
- Past turning back = {Q4 yes, Q6 after}, Q5 either.
- Those who would notice are gone = {Q4 yes, Q7 no}. keeps: stands_not_readmitted.
- Bending the rule pays / costs = the two sides of Q8: one line, not two places.
- The cost counts = {Q5 yes, Q2 the other side}: the hold on its other side with the store registered.
A place v1 lacks appears unasked: {Q1 yes, Q2 favours, Q3 no, Q4 yes, Q5 never}, "held while an uncounted loss grows" (ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss; ChoiceCountCapture.counted_outlives_loss, stored under "beyond" with no item).

THE CASE. situations.json's reward-model pipeline, from its own text: Q1 no as written ("no step reads the rule from what it selected"), not known if the pass repeats; Q4 yes and Q5 never (what responses do in use "lies beyond the raters' and the reward model's closures"); Q3 not known ("the records do not say how the raters are chosen"). So it sits in "a rule set from outside" and "drawing on what is not counted" at once. Next: row 5's two witnesses (by outside) and row 2. Missing: Q1 and Q3, the two questions that would put it in the hold.
what_it_reveals:
(a) The loops (argued; the laws sit in several Lean models). lead to rule to lead (Q1) is the hold. store to say to rule to lead to store is the loop that could turn it. The region is the hold plus four ways that second loop is not there: never connected (Q5 never: not counted), connected too late (Q6: past turning back), cut by the very thing it should register (Q7: those who would notice are gone), staffed from those ahead (Q3: judged from inside). And one loop that needs nobody to notice (Q9: the loss falls on those ahead), which v1 could not place. Five sentences for 15 boxes.

(b) The hole, located. v1 reports "no law gives an arrow INTO the hold". That is two different things. Into the hold once Q1 is yes: proved (uniform_locks, favouring_locks); v1 could not draw it because its start, "any start", is not one of the 15. Q1 itself coming to be yes: no law. Every lock law takes it as a premise, and the atlas's own open item says so ("That any actual rule reads the share it selects ... is the premise"). The nearest is the line Q8 (exact: when the capacity to bend the rule gains ground). Q3 likewise: readings only (checkers-inside). So the centre of the concern is two dotted links on a drawing where every other link has a law. A column "laws that turn this question" lists the holes by script.

(c) One place had two ways out mixed. "Not counted" holds Q5 never and Q5 not yet. Not yet changes by itself with time (row 4). Never changes only from outside (rows 2 and 5). A person asking "what can happen next" gets different answers; v1 gives one box.

(d) The cost counts is not the opposite of the hold. By turned_iff it is the hold on its other side, with the store registered. On the loop it is the same loop lit differently, which removes one good-and-bad reading from the picture without a word of denial.

(e) Dependencies across families. Q6's point of no return is family A's: FourReaders.recoverable_iff_regime in ReadOffInTime.lean, "The point of no return is the regime's", onto RegimeMargin (v1: leads-out). Q8 carries two family E cases by proved identity. Family F's threshold-reading-read-late-alternates is RuleCapture.Alternating.never_locked: Q1 yes, the rule read one step late from a start against it, lead and rule falling in turn, held neither way. A v1 checker asked for a place "rebuilt from its results but nothing held yet"; it is this loop with a delay and already has a family.

(f) One behaviour on five parts (my reading). holds-itself, all-on-one, noticers-gone, past-turning-back and ended each have a keeping law of one form, "gone, it does not come back from inside" (locked_stays; SharedCodes.outside_needed; stands_not_readmitted; kept_past_least). Family A's attraction-is-not-returning is that form for every law of change.
loses_or_risks:
1. A loop drawing claims more than is proved. Its links come from different Lean models (RuleCapture, ClosedCapture, PoolFromCourse, BeyondCoupling, ReadOffInTime), joined in places only by a reading (closed-capture checker: "each law shows one half"). One drawing suggests one model. Unless each link shows its models and each join is marked proved or a reading, the loop is LESS faithful than v1. This is the main risk.
2. The questions are a new curated layer. A badly cut question misplaces many items at once; a bad place test fails locally. Each question must cite premise ids, and one that cannot is marked a reading. Q2 (three sides) and Q6 are already strained: Q6 holds two clocks, the store's and the count's, joined by one compose entry that is a reading; if that fails they are two questions.
3. Answers multiply. Nine questions give hundreds of combinations; only sets a law speaks of may be named or drawn. A blank means "no law", not "cannot be", and must be drawn so.
4. My discipline's words would add private vocabulary and a faint verdict ("reinforcing", "balancing", "correcting"). Leave them out; verbs on links.
5. Recognition. Ren said yes to places and roads. A key of questions is drier. Place names and examples stay the door; the questions are what a place opens onto.
6. "by: outside" can read as advice. It records which premise the exit drops and nothing more.
7. Nothing here is tested on a person. Five-minute and one-hour understanding are argued.
cost_to_build:
By script from what exists.
- `by`, first cut. Transition kind: of 103 transitions, 57 (exact threshold, tipping in a parameter, critical mass) go to none; 22 (window or deadline) to a fork in time; 9 (pace bound) to sets_in; 4 (drift) to chance. Exit `drops`: 207 of 321 exits name a premise dropped, which goes to outside and names the question turned. To be checked by reading; in the codes dynamics the dropped premise is a symmetry, not a link.
- Candidate questions: premises dropped by exits (191 distinct, 45 dropped more than once; in the region closedcapture-unread five times) and premises taken by several dynamics (53 of the region's 314).
- Once `where`, `turns` and `given` exist: containment, arrows between places, the holes, the key's layout, each place's article skeleton and a case's position are all computed.

By reading.
- Parts and questions for each region (about 5 and 9; my guess for the whole atlas, 12 to 15 parts and 40 to 50 questions), against Lean statements, with a second reader to refute, as the places were.
- `turns` and `given` for each item. For the 88 the notes already say it ("holds from any start", "a boundary for a fixed group"): a re-reading of notes, not of Lean. For the 346 to come: one more field set in the adjudication already planned.
- Grouping a case's assessed premises under questions (one case exists).

Net: more than extending v1, nearly all of it in the questions. The 88 decisions are kept whole. No run, build or render is needed to try it.
scales_to_other_families:
A, Absorption and ending (29 dynamics; read 14): holds, and is this structure's home ground. Its laws are about a level, a draw, a giving, a need, a reserve: parts with amounts. margin-of-a-regime gives an exact line in the level (RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below: ends exactly where the start is below H + y), a line in the draw (tipping in a parameter), a band on the time to break (window), exit-from-a-margin by chance, slowing-down-before-an-own-end as a sign near the line. All four `by` values occur. Questions: does giving meet the draw; is the level above the line; is a feeder supported; is there a reserve. a-cascade-along-total-dependence is the same question passed along links of dependence. Strain: attraction-is-not-returning, basins-of-a-determined-law and every-loss-passes-a-juncture hold of every law of change and have no parts. They give a small base layer of behaviours (rests, cycles, returns, drawn in and not returning, ends) under all regions; they are not a region.

E, Waiting and reciprocity (10 dynamics; read all): holds, more naturally than places do, because the family is about the links: who waits on whom. Tolerance.restores_iff says a formation gives from every start exactly where no clear chain of n waits leads into it, a law about the shape of the links. Questions: memory or not; a chain of waits into it; tolerance at least the number waited on outside the set; window at least the run of errors. Its γ against β line is Q8 by proved identity. Strain: the parts are indexed (any number of formations over a relation), so the loop drawing shows a pattern (a pair, a ring, a chain), not five fixed boxes, and "a chain of length n" is not a yes or no.

F, Cycles (glanced): a link read late. late-relay-oscillates settles exactly where a + (l + 1)M ≤ b + 1. Needs the one attribute `late`; otherwise fits.

G, Rest (59 exits, no transitions; glanced): like A's general laws, behaviours of any course. The loop picture is trivial there; the schema neither helps nor harms.

Not read beyond names: B, D, H.
first_change: Write the nine questions for the first region and re-say the 15 places as answers to them: one table, 15 rows by 9 columns, each column citing its premise ids. Then check it against the 88 existing decisions: each item must turn one column, sit on one line, or be a keeps / sets_in of one row. It needs no new Lean reading. It replaces the 15 free-text tests, makes the overlaps and the missing place explicit, gives the questions to ask of a real case, and tests this proposal cheaply: if the 15 cannot be said this way, or the 88 do not each land on one column, the proposal fails and v1 stands. Typing the arrows (`by`) comes second, and its first cut is a script.
false_premise:
Three, and one in the task text.
1. "The data structure that projects onto the map" supposes one map. A person needs two pictures different in kind: what generates (the loop) and where something can be (the places). v1 is the second without the first, which is why its notes carry the structure in prose. Recognition goes by place; explanation and "what next" go by structure.
2. "Optimal" and "Pareto frontier". What can be shown is dominance on stated counts: a structure from which v1 can be regenerated, with more besides, is at least as good on understanding, faithfulness, use and scale, and worse on cost. Whether anything is optimal for human understanding, nothing here shows; a person reading decides it.
3. "No law gives an arrow into the hold" is partly an artefact of the place list. The law exists (uniform_locks); what has no law is the link from who is ahead to the rule coming to be.
4. The task's "a flat list would reach 35 to 40 places" supposes places add up across families. Parts and questions add up; places partly repeat, one behaviour on different parts.
